sn14.13:2.2: The identity of this monk is uncertain. Most manuscripts, and the commentary, simply have Kaccāna here, which is probably not “Kaccāna the Great”. Some manuscripts add a personal name, Saddha or Sandha, while the Chinese parallel at SA 457 has 婆迦利, evidently for Vakkali. He may be the Sabhiya Kaccāna who appears in the same location at [sn44.11]().
sn14.13:2.4: The problem of false enlightened ones is discussed at [dn29:4.1](), [dn33:1.6.5](), [mn11:13.6](), [mn49:30.9](), [mn104:2.5](), and [sn55.25:10.4]().
sn14.13:3.2: The appearance of “person” here anticipates the analysis of different kinds of person in the following discourses through to [sn14.29]().
